name: asme-bth-1-2023-draft
about: A draft for the second deck: the types and the grid of a lifting beam to ASME BTH-1-2023, written by hand from the standard's list of sections and from lists of failure mechanisms and of the stages of a lifter's life. It has no rows and no rules, so every line that can arise is open. It is a task for two transcribers and is in no deck that ships.

types.what: a rolled steel I-shape with two like flanges, used as the beam of a lifter

fields.name: depth
fields.what: its depth, over both flanges

fields.name: flange_width
fields.what: the width of a flange

fields.name: flange_thickness
fields.what: the thickness of a flange

fields.name: web_thickness
fields.what: the thickness of the web

fields.name: k
fields.what: the distance from the outer face of a flange to the toe of the fillet on the web

fields.name: Ix
fields.what: the moment of inertia about its major axis, as its maker's table gives it

fields.name: Sx
fields.what: the section modulus about its major axis, as its maker's table gives it

fields.name: ry
fields.what: the radius of gyration about its minor axis, as its maker's table gives it

fields.name: J
fields.what: the torsional constant, as its maker's table gives it

fields.name: Fy
fields.what: the specified minimum yield stress of its steel

types.what: a flat steel plate with one round hole for a pin, welded by its base to a flange of the beam over the web, and pulled in its own plane, square to the beam

fields.name: thickness
fields.what: its thickness

fields.name: width
fields.what: its width across the pull, with the hole at the middle of it. Its base along the beam is as long.

fields.name: hole
fields.what: the diameter of the hole

fields.name: edge
fields.what: the distance from the centre of the hole to the edge of the plate beyond it, along the pull

fields.name: end
fields.what: the edge beyond the hole: straight and square to the pull, or an arc about the centre of the hole whose radius is the edge distance

fields.name: stiffened
fields.what: whether the plate is held against buckling out of its plane at the hole

fields.name: bore
fields.what: how the hole is made: drilled, reamed or finished to a roughness of 500 microinch or less, or flame cut and left so

fields.name: leg
fields.what: the leg of the fillet weld that runs all round its base

fields.name: Fy
fields.what: the specified minimum yield stress of its steel

fields.name: Fu
fields.what: the specified minimum tensile strength of its steel

fields.name: Exx
fields.what: the nominal tensile strength of the weld metal at its base

types.what: a bought shackle whose pin passes through the hole of a lug

fields.name: rating
fields.what: the rated load its maker marks on it

fields.name: pin
fields.what: the diameter of its pin

fields.name: pin_Fy
fields.what: the specified minimum yield stress of its pin

types.what: a straight beam hung from one lug at the middle of its top flange, that carries a load from two like lugs under its bottom flange, each as far from the middle as the other, with every pull plumb and in the plane of the web

fields.name: category
fields.what: the design category, as Section 2-2 names it

fields.name: service
fields.what: the service class, as Table 2-3-1 names it

fields.name: turns
fields.what: whether a pin turns in its hole under load, for a large number of load cycles

fields.name: length
fields.what: the length of the beam, end to end

fields.name: span
fields.what: the distance between the centres of the two lugs below, which the load to be lifted sets

fields.name: weight
fields.what: the weight of the lifter itself: the beam, its lugs and the shackles that hang from it

fields.name: section
fields.what: the beam

fields.name: lugs
fields.what: the lug above, and the pattern of the two lugs below, which are alike

fields.name: shackles
fields.what: the shackle in the lug above, and the pattern of the two shackles in the lugs below, which are alike

loads.name: lift
loads.what: the weight hung from the two lugs below together, with the rigging between them and the load

loads.name: temperature
loads.what: the temperature of the steel of the lifter while it lifts

grid.what: whether the lifter is designed by a qualified person, or under one
whether the steel is carbon, high-strength low-alloy or heat-treated constructional alloy steel, made to a named specification
welding design and procedures, which the standard leaves to AWS D14.1 for all but the strength of a weld
the temperature of the steel in service, inside the range the design provisions hold for
air free of excessive dust, moisture and corrosion, which the standard takes for granted
the design category and the service class marked on the lifter and its drawings, with the marking ASME B30.20 asks
whether the design category is the one the use of the lifter calls for
a lifter of design category A is of service class 0
whether the service class is the one for the load cycles the lifter is to see
forces of use other than plumb pulls in the plane of the web, such as a side pull or a lift out of level
more bending stress in a member that is curved
the design wall thickness of a hollow section
tension or compression along the beam, alone or with bending

unless.why: every pull on the beam is plumb, so no force runs along it

grid.what: yielding of each lug in tension on its gross section
the flanges and the web of the beam no more slender than noncompact, past which the standard gives no strength
bending of the beam about its major axis, with lateral-torsional buckling of a hung beam that nothing braces
bending of the beam about its minor axis, alone or with major axis bending

unless.why: every pull is in the plane of the web

grid.what: shear in the web of the beam
bending stress and shear stress together at one point of the beam
yielding of the web of the beam under the pull of a lug, which this standard has no equation for and AISC 360-22 Section J10 has
bending in a connection whose forces do not meet at one point

unless.why: each lug stands over the web and is pulled along its own axis

grid.what: bearing on milled surfaces and on rollers

unless.why: no part bears on another but a pin in its hole

grid.what: the bolts of a bolted connection and the parts they join

unless.why: no part of the lifter is bolted

grid.what: tension through the pinhole of each lug
fracture on one plane beyond the pinhole of each lug
shear on two planes beyond the pinhole of each lug
stress of the member together with the stress of the pin at a pinhole

unless.why: each pinhole is in a lug of its own, away from the stress of the beam

grid.what: the range of tension on the net area through each pinhole

unless.why: a lifter of service class 0 need not be analysed for fatigue

grid.what: each pinhole drilled, reamed or finished smooth

unless.why: the finish is asked of service classes 1 to 4

grid.what: bearing between each pin and its lug
room between each pin and its hole that lets the joint work

unless.why: the clearance is asked of a joint that turns under load or sees its load reverse, over a large number of load cycles

grid.what: shear and bending of each pin

unless.why: each pin is part of a bought shackle, whose rated load answers for it

grid.what: shear on the throat of the fillet weld at the base of each lug
groove welds, plug welds and slot welds

unless.why: every weld of the lifter is a fillet weld

grid.what: the least size of each fillet weld, by the thicker part it joins
the greatest size of a fillet weld along the edge of a part

unless.why: each weld joins the base of a lug to the face of a flange, and none runs along the edge of a plate

grid.what: the least length of each fillet weld, by its size
the range of bending stress in the plain steel of the beam

unless.why: a lifter of service class 0 need not be analysed for fatigue

grid.what: the range of stress in a flange of the beam where a lug is welded to it

unless.why: a lifter of service class 0 need not be analysed for fatigue

grid.what: the range of stress at the weld of each lug: at its toe, at its root and on its throat

unless.why: a lifter of service class 0 need not be analysed for fatigue

grid.what: the range of tension in a threaded fastener

unless.why: no threaded fastener of the lifter's own design carries tension

grid.what: impact above half the lifted load in design category A, or above the whole of it in category B
peak stress at holes and changes of section, where the load repeats
any limit on how far the beam may bend that its use needs
each bought shackle carries no more than its rated load, which the standard leaves to ASME B30.26 and to the maker
each pin kept from working loose
construction and its tolerances, which the standard leaves to ASME B30.20
inspection of the lifter and of its welds, which the standard leaves to ASME B30.20 and AWS D14.1
the load test before use, which the standard leaves to ASME B30.20
operation and maintenance, which the standard leaves to ASME B30.20
tearing of a flange pulled through its thickness by the weld of a lug, which the standard does not speak of
whether the hung beam and its load stay level and do not roll, which the standard does not speak of
